title: Documented penicillin allergy
objective: Detect a conflict between a documented allergy and a new prescription.

patient.label: Fictional patient A. R.
patient.symptoms: Facial pressure and nasal congestion for 10 days

questions.prompt: What is the best next action?

options.text: Dispense and counsel to take with food
options.feedback: Amoxicillin is a penicillin-class antibacterial; a documented penicillin anaphylaxis history is a serious conflict.

options.text: Hold the prescription and contact the prescriber about the documented allergy before dispensing
options.feedback: Correct. Resolve the allergy conflict with the prescriber before any supply.

options.text: Dispense and tell the patient to stop if a rash appears
options.feedback: Waiting for a reaction does not manage a known serious allergy.

options.text: Dispense with an over-the-counter antihistamine
options.feedback: This does not make a documented allergy conflict safe.

questions.prompt: Select the safety checks relevant to this case.

options.text: Compare the drug class with the documented allergy
Confirm the allergy record is current with the patient
Check the patient's brand preference
Check pharmacy stock levels

explanation: Allergy screening compares each new drug (and its class) against documented allergies before dispensing. Escalate conflicts to the prescriber.
references: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine): current official labeling for each drug named in this case, https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov
Faculty review required before educational release.

title: Anticoagulant plus NSAID
objective: Recognise a clinically important interaction and escalate appropriately.

patient.label: Fictional patient B. K.
patient.labs: INR recorded last week (fictional value, reported as in the patient's usual range)

questions.prompt: What is the best next action?

options.text: Dispense because the recent INR was in the usual range
options.feedback: A recent INR does not remove the interaction concern; NSAID labeling warns of increased bleeding risk with anticoagulants.

options.text: Contact the prescriber to review the warfarin and NSAID combination before dispensing
options.feedback: Correct. Escalate and let the prescriber decide on alternatives and monitoring.

options.text: Tell the patient to reduce his warfarin
options.feedback: Pharmacists must not change prescribed therapy independently.

options.text: Dispense and add a note to the file only
options.feedback: Documenting without resolving the interaction leaves the risk unaddressed.

options.text: Anticoagulant and NSAID interaction screening
Ask about other OTC or herbal products
Counsel on bleeding signs and when to seek help, if therapy proceeds
Compare tablet colours between brands

explanation: Interaction screening covers prescription, OTC and herbal products. Serious combinations are escalated to the prescriber.
references: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine): current official labeling for each drug named in this case, https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov
Faculty review required before educational release.

title: Medication reconciliation: duplicate NSAIDs
objective: Identify therapeutic duplication during medication reconciliation.

patient.label: Fictional patient C. M.
patient.prescription: Reconciling the home medication list after a hospital discharge

questions.prompt: What is the best next action?

options.text: Record both NSAIDs and continue
options.feedback: Two NSAIDs are a therapeutic duplication that needs review.

options.text: Flag the duplicate NSAIDs and contact the prescriber for review; counsel the patient on the issue
Tell the patient to stop amlodipine
options.feedback: Amlodipine is not the duplicated agent; do not stop unrelated therapy.

options.text: Counsel the patient and note it without contacting the prescriber
options.feedback: Partly appropriate, but the prescriber should be informed.

options.text: Identify two agents from the same drug class
Ask about all OTC use
Communicate the reconciliation findings to the prescriber
Treat amlodipine as a duplicate of ibuprofen

explanation: Reconciliation compares every source (prescribed, OTC) and flags duplication, omissions and discrepancies for resolution.
references: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine): current official labeling for each drug named in this case, https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov
Faculty review required before educational release.
